ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are all on the lattice points of a square grid. What is the value of $\sin\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw BD $\perp$ AC, \\
since BC $= \sqrt{1^{2}+3^{2}} = \sqrt{10}$, and BD $= \sqrt{1^{2}+1^{2}} = \sqrt{2}$, \\
therefore, $\sin\angle ACB = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{10}} = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: I directly observe that the figure is a 3×3 square grid, A is at the lower-left lattice point, C is at the upper-right lattice point, B is on the bottom side, 2 units to the right from A, that is, 1 unit from the right side; segment AC is the main diagonal of the grid, and segment BC connects B to C. Reasoning: according to the positions in the figure, take A=(0,0), B=(2,0), C=(3,3). Draw BD perpendicular to AC, with foot D. Because the slope of AC is 1, the slope of BD perpendicular to AC is -1; the perpendicular direction from B to AC can be viewed as 1 unit left and 1 unit up, therefore BD=sqrt(1^2+1^2)=sqrt(2). At the same time, from B to C the horizontal difference is 1 unit and the vertical difference is 3 units, so BC=sqrt(1^2+3^2)=sqrt(10). In right triangle BCD, D is on AC, so angle ACB=angle DCB, therefore sin(angle ACB)=BD/BC=sqrt(2)/sqrt(10)=sqrt(5)/5.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a 3-by-3 square grid with A at the bottom-left lattice point, C at the top-right lattice point, and B on the bottom edge two grid units to the right of A and one unit left of the right side. Note that AC is the main diagonal of the square grid. Drop a perpendicular from B to AC, meeting AC at D. Since AC has slope 1, the perpendicular from B to AC has slope -1 and moves one grid unit left and one grid unit up, so BD has length sqrt(1^2+1^2)=sqrt(2). Also BC moves one grid unit right and three grid units up, so BC=sqrt(1^2+3^2)=sqrt(10). In right triangle BCD, angle ACB equals angle DCB, so sin(angle ACB)=BD/BC=sqrt(2)/sqrt(10)=sqrt(5)/5.
